title: Chapter 1: Dying House of Horrors
html:
“This is the first time I’ve ever been to a Haunted House this unscary.”

“The props are too fake; I didn’t feel scared. If anything, it all felt like a joke to me.”

“Materialists like ourselves naturally have nothing to be afraid of! Ghosts aren’t real!”

“I hate to say I told you so, but we should’ve stayed at the hostel. I was so close to leveling up in my game.”

Outside the House of Horrors in Jiujiang’s western suburbs, a group of students rode away on shared bicycles without a backward glance. Holding a stack of promotional flyers for the Haunted House, Chen Ge watched them go and shook his head helplessly.

Scaring people was an art, but after years of exposure to horror movies, modern audiences had developed a much higher tolerance for fear. For many visitors, walking through a Haunted House was no more frightening than strolling through their own backyard.

“Boss!”

A clear female voice rang out behind him. Chen Ge turned to see a petite “zombie” in a nurse’s uniform storming out of the Haunted House.

“What’s wrong, Xiao Wan?” The zombie was Xu Wan, one of the temporary actors employed by the Haunted House.

“Those jerks from earlier tried to take advantage of me!” the girl hissed through gritted teeth, her fists clenched.

So she only came to complain…

“That’s awful. They wouldn’t even leave a zombie alone.” As the boss, Chen Ge naturally took Xiao Wan’s side. “I’ll have the amusement park manager pull up the surveillance footage later.”

“There’s no need. As soon as I realized what they were trying to do, I punched one of them straight in the face.” Xu Wan pointed proudly at the bloodstain on the edge of her costume. “See? This isn’t fake blood.”

“Good, good. A girl should know how to protect herself.” Chen Ge wiped the cold sweat from his forehead. Glancing at the setting sun, he added, “I think it’s time to call it a day. We probably won’t get any more visitors, so go tell everyone they can leave early.”

However, the girl in zombie makeup made no move to leave.

“Is there anything else?”

“Boss…” Xu Wan hesitated, then slowly pulled two letters from her pocket. “These are Tao Ming’s and Xiao Wei’s resignation letters. You’ve been so good to them that they didn’t have the nerve to give them to you in person, so they asked me to pass them on.”

“They’re quitting?” Chen Ge asked, though the answer was obvious. He accepted the letters and added, “Everyone has their own dreams to chase. So be it. Xiao Wan, you can head home if there’s nothing else.”

“Okay. I’ll go remove my makeup first.”

After the cute little zombie left, Chen Ge silently lit a cigarette. Half a year earlier, his parents had mysteriously disappeared, leaving him with only this Haunted House. To keep their memory alive, he had quit his day job and devoted himself to running it.

Unfortunately, times were changing. Haunted Houses might have been a niche form of entertainment, but competition was fierce and the business had plenty of limitations. A scary scenario lost much of its impact after the first visit, yet constantly updating the attraction required a great deal of time and money.

For the past few weeks, the Haunted House had been operating in the red; daily ticket sales barely covered the water and electricity bills.

“I wonder how long I can hold on.”

After stubbing out his cigarette, Chen Ge was about to return to the Haunted House when a middle-aged man in a New Century Park uniform approached him. The moment Chen Ge saw him, he quickened his pace like a mouse spotting a cat.

“You think you can pretend you didn’t see me?” The middle-aged man clamped both hands on Chen Ge’s shoulders. “We need to settle this today. You’re already two months behind on rent and utilities. The higher-ups are breathing down my neck to collect, so pay up!”

“Uncle Xu, it’s not that I don’t want to pay you, but I really have nothing to pay you with. Can you please give me another month?”

“That’s what you told me last month!”

“I promise, this is definitely the last time!” Chen Ge thumped his chest solemnly.

“People have already moved on from Haunted Houses. Listen to me—it’s no use being this stubborn.” When Uncle Xu noticed the letters in Chen Ge’s hand, his grip on Chen Ge’s shoulders gradually loosened. “You’re still young. You can start over in another career, so why keep doing this to yourself?”

“Uncle Xu, I know you’re looking out for me, but this Haunted House means something different to me. I guess I’m still not ready to let go of the last thing my parents left behind,” Chen Ge said quietly, as though afraid someone else might hear.

As the amusement park manager, Uncle Xu knew about the disappearance of Chen Ge’s parents. He was silent for a few seconds before sighing. “Fine. I understand how you feel. I’ll talk to management and see if I can get you a few more weeks.”

“Thank you, Uncle Xu!”

“Don’t thank me yet. You’d better find a way to increase ticket sales, or things will end the same way.”

After seeing the amusement park manager off, Chen Ge returned to the Haunted House and began his daily routine of inspecting the equipment, maintaining the props, and cleaning.

“The fake blood in the maintenance room is almost gone. I’ll have to buy another batch.”

“If I angled this corridor a little more, it would create a better blind spot for scaring visitors.”

“Oh no, this puppet is already broken. I’ll have to repair it later.”

“F*ck! What happened to the lightbulb I installed here last week? Who stole it?!”

To an outsider, owning a Haunted House might have made him look like a young entrepreneur, but only Chen Ge understood how difficult the business was to maintain. A Haunted House was a form of entertainment built around controlled fear: visitors’ bodies and minds were pushed into a heightened state, and the release of that tension afterward produced a strange sense of relief and satisfaction.

Most Haunted Houses were also one-trick attractions. The easiest business model was a mobile setup that could keep moving and drawing fresh visitors. A permanent Haunted House like Chen Ge’s needed enough fame to keep attracting new crowds; otherwise, it could not survive for long. The fact that he had lasted this long was already something of a miracle.

Dragging the ruined puppet behind him, Chen Ge entered the maintenance room. He had studied toy design in college, and he had personally designed and built the machinery and traps used throughout the Haunted House. Repair work—sewing, repainting, and replacing worn parts—was tedious and repetitive.

“Still need more fake blood. If I remember correctly, there should be some left in the attic.” The Haunted House had three floors: the first two contained the attraction’s scenarios, while the third served as storage.

When he pushed open the wooden door, he found piles of supplies and discarded materials beyond a haze of sawdust and dust—things his parents had left behind from the days when they ran the Haunted House.

Unwilling to confront the past, Chen Ge rarely came up here.

“Come to think of it, it’s been almost half a year.”

The old equipment brought back memories of Chen Ge’s childhood. Back then, his family had run a mobile Haunted House, giving him the chance to travel across the country with his parents. Whenever they were busy, they left him alone backstage among the ghost props. Years of that had given him nerves far stronger than most people’s.

After all, while other children his age played with blocks and puzzles, he ran around carrying a fake human head.

“These are all precious memories.”

Chen Ge wandered aimlessly until he found himself back at the wooden box holding the few belongings his parents had left behind. Inside were a black cell phone and a crude-looking doll. The doll was the first toy Chen Ge had made as a child, but he had no memory of the phone. Both items had been found in an abandoned hospital in the countryside. As for why his parents had gone there in the middle of the night, even the police had been unable to give him an answer.

“Where are the two of you?” Chen Ge picked up the doll and pinched its chubby face. With a sigh, he told himself, “I’d better find that fake blood. If I can’t survive the off-season, I really will have to say goodbye to this Haunted House.”

Chen Ge was talking to himself, but as he spoke, the black phone lying silent in the box suddenly lit up with a dim, cold glow.

“What’s going on? Some kind of advanced technology, or a supernatural phenomenon?” Anyone else might already have run out screaming, but Chen Ge remained comparatively calm. He picked up the phone and examined it more closely.

“This is strange. I’ve tried turning this phone on more than a hundred times, and it never worked. Why did it start by itself today? It was found where my parents disappeared. Could they know I’m in trouble and be trying to help me?”

Chen Ge swiped the phone open. Against the black home screen, there was only one app, its icon shaped like a Haunted House.

“Wait… This looks familiar. It’s just like the entrance to my own Haunted House!”

Frowning, Chen Ge opened the app. A line of text that looked as though it had been written in blood appeared on the screen—Do you believe there are ghosts in this world?

Objectively speaking, it was a metaphysical question. For an engineering student like Chen Ge, it was practically impossible to answer.

“There should be,” Chen Ge murmured. A few seconds later, another sentence appeared on the screen.

“What you believe is the answer. From this moment on, you will officially take over as the new owner of the Haunted House. Of course, this is hardly something worth celebrating. Before the tutorial ends, heed my final advice: taking your own life is the most cowardly choice. Do everything you can to survive!”

“What is that supposed to mean? Still, that pompous tone does sound like my father.”

Chen Ge clicked on the app again, and a new window appeared.

_______________

Western Jiujiang Haunted House

Status: Almost Closing

Good Reputation: Zero

Daily Visitor Number: Four

Monthly Visitor Number: Ten

My Team of Ghosts and Ghouls: None

My Item Storage: None

Unlocked Achievement: None

Current Available Scenarios [Set Pieces]:

– Night of the Living Dead – Terrible props, untrained actors, and a plot with neither story nor logic. Scream Factor: 0 Stars

– Minghun [Netherworld Marriage] – A couple torn apart in life, bound together forever in the netherworld; sharing one grave and seeking happiness in death. Scream Factor: 0.5 Stars

Unlockable Scenarios:

– Murder by Midnight – A dangerous psychiatric patient roams a dilapidated apartment building. Armed with scissors and a hammer, he is pacing outside your door. Scream Factor: 1 Star

– The Third Sick Hall – Strange sounds emerge from this abandoned hospital every night. As a newspaper reporter, you have been sent inside to uncover the truth. Scream Factor: 3 Stars

– The Haunted Hearse – A hearse carrying the dead has already set off. If you cannot escape within an hour, you will remain aboard forever. Scream Factor: 2 Stars

Daily Mission: Complete the Haunted House’s Daily Missions to receive rewards and unlock more terrifying scenarios. Rewards correspond to mission difficulty.

Haunted House Expansion Conditions: Monthly Visitors above 100. Positive Rating above 60 percent. (After three expansions, the Haunted House will upgrade to The Shivering Maze.)

Haunted Wheel of Misfortune (Spend Fright Points generated by Haunted House visitors to spin the Wheel): Life and death are decreed by fate; fortune and misfortune lie only a hair apart. The Wheel contains Spirit Fruits that can extend your lifespan—as well as Baleful Specters overflowing with hatred!

Other Functions: Not Yet Unlocked
